explain.es: El subjuntivo inglés no tiene terminaciones propias: es la forma base del verbo (be, go, pay) usada con cualquier sujeto y cualquier tiempo, o bien la forma were para todas las personas. Por eso casi no se ve: solo lo delatan la 3.ª persona sin -s (that he go), el verbo be (that they be) y la negación sin do (that she not attend). A diferencia del español, donde el subjuntivo es omnipresente (quiero que vengas), en inglés es un recurso marcado: propio de contratos, actas, normativas, informes, prensa seria y del inglés americano. Dominarlo —y saber cuándo sustituirlo por should o por el indicativo— es una señal inequívoca de nivel C2.
explain.en: The English subjunctive is simply the base form of the verb (or were), used regardless of person or tense. It is only visible in the third person singular, with be and in negatives. It belongs to formal, legal and academic registers and is more common in American English.
formula: Verbo / adjetivo / nombre de mandato + *that* + sujeto + *forma base*
Fórmulas fijas + *Be that as it may · Come what may*

explain.title: 1 · Subjuntivo mandativo: verbos
explain.es: Tras verbos que expresan orden, exigencia, propuesta o recomendación —insist, demand, require, request, recommend, suggest, propose, urge, ask, order, advise, stipulate, direct, move— la cláusula con that lleva el verbo en forma base, sea cual sea el sujeto y sea cual sea el tiempo del verbo principal: no hay concordancia de tiempos (They insisted that he be…). That puede omitirse en registro menos formal (I suggest you go), pero tras suggest, insist o demand nunca se usa objeto + to-infinitivo.
explain.en: After verbs of ordering, demanding, proposing or recommending, the that-clause takes the base form for every person and with any tense in the main clause. Never use object + to after suggest, insist or demand.
formula: insist / demand / recommend + *that* + he / she / they + *be / go / pay*

examples.en: The union demanded that the agreement be made public.
examples.es: El sindicato exigió que el acuerdo se hiciera público.

examples.en: Her lawyer insisted that she remain silent during questioning.
examples.es: Su abogado insistió en que guardara silencio durante el interrogatorio.

examples.en: I move that the motion be put to a vote.
examples.es: Propongo que la moción se someta a votación.

explain.title: 2 · Con adjetivos y sustantivos
explain.es: El mismo patrón aparece tras adjetivos de necesidad o importancia en la estructura It is + adjetivo + that (essential, vital, imperative, crucial, necessary, important, advisable, desirable, paramount) y tras sustantivos derivados de los verbos mandativos (the demand / requirement / recommendation / proposal / insistence that…). Ojo: con adjetivos de opinión o emoción (odd, surprising, sad, a pity) no se usa el subjuntivo de forma base, sino el indicativo o should (regla 4).
explain.en: The same pattern follows adjectives of necessity or importance (It is essential / vital / imperative that…) and nouns derived from mandative verbs (the requirement that…). Adjectives of emotion take the indicative or should instead.
formula: It is + *essential / vital / imperative* + that + sujeto + *base*

examples.en: It is imperative that every passenger carry valid identification.
examples.es: Es imprescindible que todo pasajero lleve un documento de identidad válido.

examples.en: It was vital that the patient receive treatment within the hour.
examples.es: Era vital que el paciente recibiera tratamiento en menos de una hora.

examples.en: The requirement that applicants be fluent in two languages was dropped.
examples.es: Se eliminó el requisito de que los candidatos dominaran dos idiomas.

explain.title: 3 · Negativa, pasiva y be
explain.es: En la negativa se coloca not delante del verbo base, sin do: that he not be, that they not leave (that he doesn't leave en registro formal; that he be not es arcaico). En pasiva, el subjuntivo es be + participio para todas las personas: that the results be published. Es la combinación más frecuente en informes y normativas. Existen también, aunque son raras, formas con aspecto: that he be working, that she have completed.
explain.en: Negatives place not before the base form, with no do. The passive is be + past participle for every person — the most frequent pattern in reports and regulations.

examples.en: The committee recommended that the proposal not be approved.
examples.es: El comité recomendó que no se aprobara la propuesta.

examples.en: We ask that mobile phones be switched off throughout the performance.
examples.es: Rogamos que se apaguen los móviles durante toda la función.

examples.en: It is essential that candidates not have any criminal record.
examples.es: Es imprescindible que los candidatos no tengan antecedentes penales.

explain.title: Tres registros, una misma idea
head: Disparador · Trigger
🎩 Subjuntivo (formal / US)
🫖 Should (formal UK)
💬 Indicativo (coloquial UK)
🇪🇸 Español
rows: They insisted that he should be paid.
Insistieron en que se le pagara.
I recommend that she take a break.
I recommend that she should take a break.
I recommend that she takes a break.
Recomiendo que se tome un descanso.
It's essential that he should be told.
Es esencial que se lo digan.
explain.note: Las tres columnas existen en inglés británico, pero no valen para cualquier texto: en un examen C2, un informe o un contrato, elige el subjuntivo o should. Además, el indicativo con el verbo principal en pasado puede ser ambiguo: They insisted that he was paid también significa «aseguraron que sí se le había pagado».
explain.note_en: All three exist in British English, but the indicative is informal and can be ambiguous: They insisted that he was paid may also mean they claimed he had been paid.

explain.title: Formal, neutro o coloquial
explain.es: La misma idea en tres registros. En C2 se espera que sepas subir y bajar de registro a voluntad: el subjuntivo es la herramienta más clara para «subir».
explain.en: The same idea in three registers. At C2 you must be able to move up and down at will; the subjunctive is the clearest way to sound formal.

cols.head: 🎩 Formal / escrito
items: The board requires that all expenses be approved.
Were I in your position, I would decline.
Should you need assistance, please let us know.
Be that as it may, the rule stands.

cols.head: 🙂 Neutro
items: The board says all expenses must be approved.
If I were you, I'd say no.
If you need any help, just let us know.
Even so, the rule stands.

cols.head: 💬 Coloquial
items: The board wants every expense OK'd first.
If I was you, I'd say no.
Need a hand? Give me a shout.
Still, rules are rules.

explain.title: 4 · Should formal y should «emotivo»
explain.es: En inglés británico, la alternativa más habitual al subjuntivo mandativo es should + infinitivo (They proposed that the meeting should be postponed). Además, should aparece tras adjetivos, nombres y verbos de emoción, sorpresa o juicio (odd, strange, surprising, natural, a pity, a shame, I'm amazed that…): es el should putativo, que presenta la idea como algo que se valora, no como un simple hecho. Suele corresponder a nuestro subjuntivo: Es raro que diga eso → It's odd that he should say that. Por último, If … should expresa una posibilidad poco probable («si por casualidad»); en cartas formales se invierte: Should you require…
explain.en: British English often uses should + infinitive instead of the mandative subjunctive. Putative should follows words of emotion or judgement (odd, a pity, surprising, natural). If … should marks an unlikely possibility.
formula: It's + *odd / a pity / natural* + that + sujeto + *should* + infinitivo

examples.en: It's a pity that you should feel that way about it.
examples.es: Es una pena que lo veas así.

examples.en: I find it extraordinary that nobody should have noticed the error.
examples.es: Me parece increíble que nadie se diera cuenta del error.

examples.en: If you should require any further information, do not hesitate to contact us.
examples.es: Si necesitara más información, no dude en ponerse en contacto con nosotros.

explain.title: 5 · El subjuntivo con were
explain.es: Were se usa con todas las personas (también I / he / she / it) en situaciones irreales o hipotéticas: tras if, as if / as though, I wish, if only, suppose. En el habla, was es muy frecuente (If I was you…), pero en registro formal y escrito se prefiere were. Dos usos típicos de C2: were to + infinitivo, para hipótesis remotas o delicadas (If the government were to fall…), y were it not for / if it were not for (= de no ser por). La inversión Were I… se trabaja a fondo en C1-01.
explain.en: Were is used for every person in unreal or hypothetical clauses (if, as if, wish, suppose); was is informal. Note were to for remote hypotheses and were it not for (= without).

examples.en: If the chairman were to resign, the share price would collapse.
examples.es: Si el presidente dimitiera, la cotización se hundiría.

examples.en: Were it not for her diplomacy, the talks would break down.
examples.es: De no ser por su diplomacia, las negociaciones se romperían.

examples.en: He behaves as though he were above the law.
examples.es: Se comporta como si estuviera por encima de la ley.

explain.title: Fórmulas fijas con subjuntivo
head: Fórmula · Formula
Significado · Meaning
🇪🇸 Equivalente
Ejemplo · Example
rows: Be that as it may, the deadline stands.
Come what may, we'll finish the project.
Que así sea / Pues muy bien
If they want a fight, so be it.
Suffice it to say, he wasn't invited again.
I don't wish to… (but I will)
Far be it from me to criticise, but…
We'll work overnight if need be.
She became, as it were, a stranger at home.
Heaven forbid that it should rain!
Truth be told, I never liked him.
whether it is X or Y
Be it in print or online, accuracy matters.
The powers that be have vetoed it.
Woe betide anyone who arrives late.
explain.note: Son bloques fijos: no se conjugan ni se «modernizan» (Come what it may, Be as it may, Long lives the King). Muchas suenan literarias, solemnes o irónicas: úsalas con moderación y en el registro adecuado.
explain.note_en: These are fixed blocks: never conjugate or alter them. Many sound literary, solemn or ironic, so use them sparingly.

explain.title: 6 · Lest y concesivas con be
explain.es: Lest (muy formal o literario) significa para que no / no sea que y va seguido de forma base o de should: lest he forget, lest it should be misunderstood; nunca de would. Tras fear, be afraid, be terrified equivale a «por miedo a que»: She was terrified lest anyone discover the truth. En registro neutro se dice in case o so that … not. Por otro lado, las concesivas con be (whether it be … or …, be they rich or poor) dan un tono solemne o retórico.
explain.en: Lest (very formal) means so that … not or for fear that, and takes the base form or should, never would. Neutral alternatives: in case, so that … not. Concessive be clauses sound rhetorical.

examples.es: Apúntalo para que no se te olvide.

examples.en: We must act now, lest history repeat itself.

examples.en: All citizens, whether they be rich or poor, are equal before the law.

items.es: La presidenta propuso que se aprobara sin modificaciones el acta de la reunión anterior.

items.en: Ms Patel requested that her objection to item 4 be recorded.
items.es: La Sra. Patel solicitó que constara en acta su objeción al punto 4.

items.en: The auditors had recommended that the accounts be resubmitted by 30 June.

items.bad: I suggest you to apply for the post.
items.good: I suggest (that) you apply for the post.
items.why: Suggest + that + sujeto + base (o suggest applying), nunca + to.

items.bad: I insist on that you stay.
items.why: Calco de «insisto en que»: sin on delante de that.

items.bad: The panel recommended that the drug be not licensed.
items.why: Not va delante de be; be not es arcaico.

items.bad: <small>(informe)</small> We recommend that the policy is reviewed annually.
items.good: We recommend that the policy be / should be reviewed annually.
items.why: En un informe, subjuntivo o should; el indicativo es coloquial.

items.bad: The lawyer insisted that his client be innocent.
items.good: The lawyer insisted that his client was innocent.

items.bad: He tiptoed out lest he would wake the baby.
items.good: He tiptoed out lest he wake / should wake the baby.
items.why: Lest + forma base o should; nunca would.
items.why_en: Lest + base form or should, never would.

items.bad: Come what it may, I'll support you.
items.why: Las fórmulas fijas no se tocan: no añadas sujeto.

items.es: Localiza el disparador: ¿hay un verbo, adjetivo o nombre de exigencia, necesidad o recomendación (insist, essential, requirement)?
items.en: Find the trigger: a verb, adjective or noun of demand, necessity or recommendation.

items.es: Comprueba el significado: insist / suggest = exigir / proponer → subjuntivo; = afirmar / insinuar → indicativo.
items.en: Check the meaning: demand → subjunctive; claim or imply → indicative.

items.es: Escribe that + sujeto + forma base: sin -s, sin -ed y sin cambio de tiempo aunque el verbo principal esté en pasado.
items.en: Write that + subject + base form: no -s, no -ed, no backshift.

items.es: ¿Negativa? → not + base. ¿Pasiva? → be + participio.
items.en: Negative → not + base. Passive → be + participle.

items.es: Elige el registro: subjuntivo (formal / US), should (formal UK) o indicativo (coloquial).
items.en: Choose the register: subjunctive, should or indicative.

items.es: Revisa: ¿hay <s>to</s> tras suggest / demand? ¿hay <s>do / does</s> en la negativa? ¿<s>on</s> delante de that? ¡Fuera!
items.en: Check: no to after suggest / demand, no do in negatives, no on before that.

explain.title: Truco de registro
explain.es: Pregúntate quién va a leer el texto. ¿Contrato, acta, normativa, informe o redacción de examen? → subjuntivo (o should). ¿Email a un compañero o conversación? → indicativo o una paráfrasis (They want him to…, He has to…). Atajo para el examen: tras essential, vital, recommend, demand, require, la forma base (be, go, not attend) nunca es incorrecta en registro formal.
explain.en: Ask who will read the text: contracts, minutes, reports and exam essays → subjunctive or should; emails and conversation → indicative or a paraphrase. After essential, vital, recommend, demand, require, the base form is always safe in formal writing.

items.q: In the mandative subjunctive, the verb changes according to the tense of the main clause.
items.why: Siempre forma base: They insisted that he be…

items.q: If I was you is common in speech, but If I were you is preferred in formal writing.
The negative subjunctive is formed with do not + base form.
items.why: Es not + base, sin do: that he not attend.

items.q: Should + infinitive is a typically British alternative to the mandative subjunctive.
He insisted that he be innocent means that he claimed he was innocent.
items.why: Para afirmar, indicativo: insisted that he was innocent.

items.q: Lest means ‘so that … not’ and is very formal.
Come what may can also be written Come what it may.
Suggest can be followed by object + to-infinitive: I suggest you to go.
items.why: I suggest (that) you go / I suggest going.

items.q: In Were it not for the rain, we'd go out, were is a subjunctive form.
The mandative subjunctive is more widely used in American English than in British English.

exercises.en: Put the tiles in order and write the sentence.

items.q: that / insisted / she / be / they / informed
items.a: They insisted that she be informed.

items.q: essential / is / it / that / he / attend / the meeting
items.a: It is essential that he attend the meeting.

items.q: recommend / we / not / that / the project / be / abandoned
items.a: We recommend that the project not be abandoned.

items.q: were / if / I / in / your shoes, / I'd / resign
items.a: If I were in your shoes, I'd resign.

items.q: may / be / as / that / it, / we / must / go on
items.a: Be that as it may, we must go on.

items.q: what / come / may, / I / will / support / you
items.a: Come what may, I will support you.

items.q: for / his injury, / were / it / not / he / would / be playing / today
items.a: Were it not for his injury, he would be playing today.

items.q: lest / the evidence / be / destroyed / guarded / the room / was
items.a: The room was guarded lest the evidence be destroyed.

exercises.title: Del coloquial al formal
exercises.es: Reescribe cada frase en registro formal empezando como indica la pista. Se acepta también should + infinitivo.
exercises.en: Rewrite each sentence in formal English, starting as the hint shows. Should + infinitive is also accepted.

items.q: The boss wants everyone to wear a tie.
items.a: The boss insists that everyone (should) wear a tie.

items.q: You have to bring your passport — it's essential.
items.a: It is essential that you (should) bring your passport.

items.q: They told him he had to leave the room at once.
items.a: They demanded that he (should) leave the room immediately.

items.q: Why don't you have a word with a lawyer?
items.a: I suggest (that) you consult a lawyer.

items.q: Please don't tell anyone about this — we're asking you.
items.a: We request that you not disclose this to anyone. / We request that this not be disclosed to anyone.

items.q: The new law says firms have to publish their gender pay gap.
items.a: The new law stipulates that firms (should) publish their gender pay gap.

items.q: If you need any help, just give us a ring.
items.a: Should you require any assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us.

items.q: Still, we've got to stick to the plan.
items.a: Be that as it may, we must adhere to the plan.

items.q: Whatever happens, I'll be there for you.
items.a: Come what may, I will be there for you.

items.q: Let's put the meeting off — that's what I'm proposing.
items.a: I propose that the meeting be postponed.

exercises.title: Caza el error
exercises.es: Cada frase tiene UN error (gramática o registro formal). Escríbela bien.
exercises.en: Each sentence has ONE mistake. Write it correctly.

items.q: The manager suggested us to take the day off.
items.a: The manager suggested (that) we (should) take the day off.

items.q: I insist on that you be present at the hearing.
items.a: I insist that you be present at the hearing.

items.q: The panel recommended that the drug be not licensed.
items.a: The panel recommended that the drug not be licensed.

items.q: Be as it may, the decision has been made.
items.a: Be that as it may, the decision has been made.

items.q: If I would be in your position, I'd apologise.
items.a: If I were in your position, I'd apologise.

items.q: She tiptoed out lest she would wake the baby.
items.a: She tiptoed out lest she (should) wake the baby.

items.q: The lawyer insisted that his client be at home that night.
items.a: The lawyer insisted that his client was at home that night.

items.q: Long lives the King!
items.a: Long live the King!

items.q: It's a pity that he should feels so lonely.
items.a: It's a pity that he should feel so lonely.

items.q: They demanded him to return the money.
items.a: They demanded that he (should) return the money.

exercises.title: Transformaciones (Cambridge C2)
exercises.es: Completa la segunda frase para que signifique lo mismo que la primera. Usa la palabra clave (entre paréntesis) sin cambiarla, y entre 3 y 8 palabras.
exercises.en: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the key word without changing it, and between three and eight words.

items.q:
All visitors must sign in at reception.
→ It ________ sign in at reception.
items.a: It is essential that all visitors sign in at reception.

items.q:
‘You really must see a specialist,’ the GP told Ana.
→ The GP ________ a specialist.
items.a: The GP insisted that Ana (should) see a specialist.

items.q:
Without your support, the charity would have to close.
→ ________ your support, the charity would have to close.
items.a: Were it not for / If it were not for your support, the charity would have to close.

items.q:
The union wants the agreement to be published in full.
→ The union is ________ in full.
items.a: The union is demanding that the agreement (should) be published in full.

items.q:
Nevertheless, the board's decision is final.
→ Be ________, the board's decision is final.
items.a: Be that as it may, the board's decision is final.

items.q:
I don't want to interfere, but I think you're making a mistake.
→ Far ________, but I think you're making a mistake.
items.a: Far be it from me to interfere, but I think you're making a mistake.

items.q:
Take a map in case you get lost.
→ Take a map ________ lost.
items.a: Take a map lest you (should) get lost.

items.q:
Imagine the dam bursting: it would be a catastrophe.
→ If the dam ________ be a catastrophe.
items.a: If the dam were to burst, it would be a catastrophe.

items.q:
Visitors were asked not to touch the exhibits.
→ It was requested ________ the exhibits.
items.a: It was requested that visitors (should) not touch the exhibits.

items.q:
The minister proposed scrapping the tax.
→ The minister put forward ________ scrapped.
items.a: The minister put forward a proposal that the tax be scrapped.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee la noticia. Marca T (true) o F (false) y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the article. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: After months of protest, Westbrook Council has finally bowed to residents' demands that the old library be preserved as a community centre. Campaigners had insisted that no decision be taken until an independent survey had been carried out, and the council, somewhat reluctantly, agreed to wait.

The survey, published last week, recommends that the building be restored rather than demolished, and stipulates that any future development not alter its Victorian façade. ‘It is vital that the character of the town be protected,’ said its author, Dr Helen Ward. ‘Were it not for the residents' persistence, this landmark would be little more than rubble by now.’

Not everyone is delighted. Councillor Mark Hughes, who had proposed that the site be sold to developers, described the outcome as ‘an expensive exercise in nostalgia’. ‘Be that as it may,’ he conceded, ‘the people have spoken, and so be it. I would only ask that the council keep a close eye on costs, lest the project become a burden on taxpayers.’

items.q: The council agreed to wait for the survey, though not enthusiastically.
The survey recommends demolishing the building.
items.why: It recommends that the building be restored rather than demolished.

items.q: According to Dr Ward, the residents' campaign saved the library.
items.why: ‘Were it not for the residents' persistence…’

items.q: Councillor Hughes intends to keep fighting the decision.
Find four verbs in the text that trigger the mandative subjunctive.
items.a: insisted, recommends, stipulates, proposed (also: ask)

items.q: Why does the text say ‘not alter’ and not ‘doesn't alter’?
items.a: Because the negative subjunctive is not + base form, without do.

items.q: Rewrite ‘Were it not for the residents' persistence’ beginning with ‘If…’.
items.a: If it were not (weren't) for the residents' persistence, …

items.q: Paraphrase ‘lest the project become a burden on taxpayers’ in neutral English.
items.a: so that the project doesn't become a burden on taxpayers / in case the project becomes a burden

items.q: Which two formulaic subjunctive expressions does Councillor Hughes use?
items.a: Be that as it may; so be it.

exercises.title: Traduce al inglés
exercises.es: Traduce al inglés en registro formal. Piensa: ¿hay un disparador? ¿forma base, should o were?

items.q: Insisto en que te quedes a cenar.
items.a: I insist that you stay for dinner.

items.q: Es imprescindible que el informe se entregue antes del lunes.
items.a: It is imperative that the report (should) be submitted before Monday.

items.q: El médico le recomendó que no condujera.
items.a: The doctor recommended that he (should) not drive.

items.q: Si yo fuera tú, no firmaría ese contrato.
items.a: If I were you, I wouldn't sign that contract.

items.q: Pase lo que pase, seguiremos adelante.
items.a: Come what may, we will carry on.

items.q: Sea como sea, la decisión ya está tomada.
items.a: Be that as it may, the decision has already been made.

items.q: Exigieron que se les devolviera el dinero.
items.a: They demanded that their money be refunded.

items.q: Es lógico que estén preocupados.
items.a: It is (only) natural that they should be worried.

items.q: De no ser por tu ayuda, no podría seguir adelante.
items.a: Were it not for (If it were not for) your help, I could not carry on.

items.q: Llévate un paraguas, no sea que llueva.
items.a: Take an umbrella lest it (should) rain / in case it rains.

items.q: La ley exige que todos los ocupantes del vehículo lleven puesto el cinturón.
items.a: The law requires that all occupants of the vehicle wear a seat belt.

items.q: Propongo que se levante la sesión.
items.a: I move (propose) that the meeting be adjourned.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe en registro formal. Usa las estructuras indicadas.
exercises.en: Write in formal English using the structures given.

items.q: Escribe dos normas para una biblioteca universitaria con require that e It is essential that.
items.a: Ej.: The library requires that users show their card. It is essential that phones be kept on silent.

items.q: Redacta la recomendación final de un informe sobre teletrabajo con recommend that … be.
items.a: Ej.: We recommend that remote working be extended to all departments.

items.q: Escribe una frase con Were it not for… sobre una persona importante para ti.
items.a: Ej.: Were it not for my grandmother, I would not be the reader I am today.

items.q: Usa Be that as it may para rebatir un argumento con el que no estás de acuerdo.
items.a: Ej.: Tourism undoubtedly brings wealth. Be that as it may, its environmental cost is unsustainable.

items.q: Escribe una frase con lest y reescríbela después en registro neutro.
items.a: Ej.: We must remain vigilant lest such crimes be repeated. → …so that such crimes don't happen again.

checklist.es: Sé formar el subjuntivo mandativo: insist that he be, demand that she go.
checklist.en: I can form the mandative subjunctive.

checklist.es: Uso not + base y be + participio, sin do ni cambio de tiempo.
checklist.en: I form negatives and passives correctly, with no do and no backshift.

checklist.es: Elijo entre subjuntivo, should e indicativo según el registro.
checklist.en: I choose between subjunctive, should and indicative according to register.
I distinguish insist = demand from insist = claim.

checklist.es: Uso were, were to y were it not for en registro formal.
checklist.en: I use were, were to and were it not for in formal writing.

checklist.es: Domino las fórmulas fijas: be that as it may, come what may, suffice it to say…
checklist.en: I can use the fixed subjunctive formulae.

checklist.es: Nunca escribo <s>suggest you to</s>, <s>demand him to</s> ni <s>insist on that</s>.
checklist.en: I never write suggest you to, demand him to or insist on that.
